note: Every entry here was found by direct live verification against a real running APEX 26.1 instance, not inferred from documentation. This is a structured index of facts already documented in prose across docs/grammar-assumptions.md and inline source comments -- see the 'source' field on each entry for the full story. This file is documentation, not (yet) wired into any runtime warning mechanism -- see docs/ecosystem-roadmap.md for why that's a deliberate scoping decision, not an oversight.

quirks.issue: getRecords() and getModel() throw a runtime error instead of returning data, even though both methods exist on the widget's method list.
quirks.evidence: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'each'), thrown from inside APEX's own modelViewBase.min.js. Confirmed twice: immediately after navigation, and again after an awaited refresh() -- not a timing fluke.
quirks.workaround: Use getPageInfo(), getSelectedRecords()/setSelectedRecords(), or a DOM locator (find a card by index or contained text) instead of getRecords()/getModel().

quirks.issue: Checking page.url() once immediately after waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded') is a race condition against an async/AJAX-driven login redirect -- the check can run before the URL actually changes, reporting failure on a login that actually succeeded.
quirks.evidence: A run that threw 'URL unchanged after submit' had its failure screenshot show the user already logged in on the real post-login dashboard. An earlier, wrong diagnosis ('Enter-key submission is unreliable, switch to a button click') was tried first and also failed the same way -- the bug was in success-detection timing, not the submission method.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample File Upload and Download app (second, independent APEX 26.1 app)
quirks.workaround: Wait for an actual URL change (page.waitForURL(url => url !== loginUrl, { timeout })) instead of a single point-in-time check after waitForLoadState.

quirks.issue: Playwright's toBeVisible()/toBeHidden() are unsafe against these elements. Even with the correct u-visible CSS class applied, the element's rendered height stayed exactly 0px when the message was triggered by calling apex.message.showPageSuccess()/showErrors() directly (bypassing a real form submission) -- confirmed stuck, not a transient animation, checked repeatedly over 1.8s.
quirks.evidence: getComputedStyle showed display:block, visibility:visible, opacity:1, height:0px simultaneously. Because the box is always zero-height in this app/theme, toBeHidden() would ALSO trivially pass even while a message genuinely is showing -- unsafe in both directions.
quirks.workaround: Assert the u-visible/u-hidden CSS class directly (toHaveClass(/u-visible/)) instead of rendered visibility.
quirks.status: worked around, root cause (why height stays 0 under direct invocation) not diagnosed

quirks.issue: Search/sort/pagination internals are implemented as _-prefixed methods on the underlying widget instance (jQuery-UI-widget-factory convention) -- there is no public, documented way to drive them via a JS method call.
quirks.evidence: Enumerated the widget instance's full prototype method list live: only refresh, openDialogChat, openInlineChat, closeChat are public (non-underscore). Everything else (_search, _paginate, _reset, _download, ...) is private by convention. Separately, apex.region(id).call(action) -- the generic action-dispatch API -- was tested with a dozen plausible action names (refresh, search, getViews, getCurrentView, reset, collapse, ...) and rejected every one with "Call not supported."
quirks.workaround: Use the generic ApexRegion methods (refresh, getViewName, getSessionState) for what they support. Drive search/sort/pagination through the actual UI (fill the visible search input, click pagination links) via Playwright locators -- not a JS API call.
quirks.status: confirmed, permanent constraint (not a bug to fix, a real API boundary)

quirks.issue: Calling fetchCounts() and immediately reading getTotalResourceCount() is unreliable -- the count can still return null. This holds even in a genuinely fresh Playwright browser context, not just a warmed/reused tab.
quirks.evidence: Discovered the real fix by monkey-patching $.fn.trigger to log every event actually fired during fetchCounts(): apexbeforerefresh then apexafterrefresh fire directly on the region's own DOM element once the async count-fetch completes.
quirks.workaround: Use fetchCountsAndWait() instead of fetchCounts() -- waits for the real apexafterrefresh event before resolving, verified reliable across 3 repeated live runs.

quirks.component: APEX client lifecycle events (apexbeforerefresh, apexafterrefresh, and likely others)
quirks.issue: These are jQuery custom events, not native DOM CustomEvents. A plain element.addEventListener('apexafterrefresh', ...) never fires.
quirks.evidence: Confirmed live: only apex.jQuery(el).on()/.trigger() -- not addEventListener/dispatchEvent -- sees these events.
quirks.workaround: Always use apex.jQuery (Oracle's documented stable reference, not a bare global $/jQuery) to listen for these events, never native addEventListener.

quirks.component: Region identifiers (all region types probed so far)
quirks.issue: The DOM/runtime id apex.region() resolves against does not match any straightforward transform of the .apx declared static id (verbatim, R_ prefix, data-region-id, data-static-id all ruled out). Runtime ids observed were numeric hash-like strings (e.g. R14614638417487636), not human-readable.
quirks.evidence: Oracle's own docs state static ids are mandatory and 'sensible' when auto-assigned, but the observed runtime ids don't look sensible/human-readable at all -- open tension, not yet resolved.
quirks.workaround: Do not assume a region's DOM/runtime id equals its .apx identifier. Obtain the runtime id by other means (read off the live DOM) until the convention is confirmed.

quirks.issue: Pages using a modal dialog page mode return HTTP 400 on a plain friendly-URL GET, instead of loading normally.
quirks.evidence: Confirmed live on p00420 (Data Entry -- Drawer Form) -- 4 generated tests fail this way, consistently, out of 43 total.
quirks.workaround: None yet -- these pages likely need a parent-page/dialog-opening context that neither the generator nor gotoApexPage constructs today.
